curriculumDefinition.commandsAndConcepts: `m{char}`; `'` and backtick jumps; special marks such as `'.`, ```.```, `'^`, ```^```, `'[`, `']`; `Ctrl-o`, `Ctrl-i`; `g;`, `g,`; `gi`, `gv`; advanced bracket/section motions
curriculumDefinition.learningOutcome: Leave a position, work somewhere else, and return to it — by mark, by jump, by change, by insertion, or by selection
curriculumDefinition.representativeExercises: Mark two sites and shuttle between them; inspect a distant definition and return; revisit the last change; resume the last insertion
curriculumDefinition.priorityAndPortability: Core through marks, the jump list, and the change list. Bracket marks and code-section motions are advanced, and the section motions read boundaries out of file syntax. All are native Vim; a host editor that embeds Vim may claim `Ctrl-o` and `Ctrl-i` for its own navigation, so check the host you are in

lessons.title: Set and use local marks
lessons.objective: Store positions and choose linewise or exact returns.

activities.title: Save a position with a mark
activities.body: Press `ma` to save the current position as mark `a`. Press `'a` to return to its line or `` `a `` to return to its exact column.
activities.grammar: m{letter} -> remember; quote -> row; backtick -> exact spot
activities.contrast: These lessons use lowercase marks because the editor has one buffer.

lessons.title: Walk jump history

activities.title: Move backward and forward through jumps
activities.body: Press `Ctrl-o` to visit older jump positions and `Ctrl-i` to move forward again. `''` returns to the previous line, while two backticks return to the exact previous position.
activities.grammar: Ctrl-o -> older; Ctrl-i -> newer; doubled quote/backtick -> previous context
activities.contrast: Small local movement does not create the same trail.

lessons.trackNote: Advanced and less commonly used: the bracket marks earn their keep for `` `[v`] ``, which reselects what you just put, but most editing days never reach for them.

activities.contrast: These marks describe operated text rather than the current selection.

lessons.title: Navigate code structure
lessons.objective: Use representative section, block, and method boundary motions.
lessons.trackNote: Advanced and less commonly used: these motions read boundaries out of the file's own syntax, so how well they land depends on the language and on how the code is laid out.

activities.title: Move between large code structures
activities.body: Bracket motions can find sections, unmatched brackets, and brace-delimited methods. Use them only when the file has clear matching structure.
activities.grammar: section boundaries; enclosing blocks; method boundaries
activities.contrast: These textual motions require deliberately unambiguous structure.

activities.title: Leave a position and come back to it
activities.body: Marks, jump history, change history, and the structural motions are four answers to one question: how do you get back to where the work is?
takeaways: Set a lowercase mark before you leave a site you plan to return to.
Use Ctrl-o and Ctrl-i for the jumps you made, g; and g, for the edits you made.
gi resumes the last insertion and gv restores the last selection.
Reach for the section and method motions only where the file's structure is unambiguous.

reference.purpose: Save a local position and return linewise or exactly.

notes: Small local motions do not create the same trail.

reference.purpose: Return to the last change, Insert exit, or Visual selection.
notes: Change and insertion history can differ.

reference.purpose: Reach the boundaries of changed or yanked text.
Walk older or newer edit positions.
Move through unambiguous large textual structure.
notes: Comment and preprocessor motions are excluded.
